description: Run a shell command on one of your Prized boxes and return its exit code, stdout and stderr when it ends. It runs under sh -c as your box user, in your home directory unless cwd says otherwise, with the tools set up on the box on PATH. A paused box is woken first, which spends the workspace's money: it bills while awake until it pauses again (longer for a box in deep sleep). A non-zero exit code is a result, not a tool error. Each stream is cut to its first 5,000 and last 15,000 characters. It is killed after timeout_seconds (default 240, at most 600). For a longer job, start it in the background (nohup cmd > log.txt 2>&1 &) and check on it later; the box's auto-pause may pause an idle box with it. A box is a persistent machine with your person's files and credentials on it: run only what they asked for.

box.description: The box: its name (such as mango) or its id, from list_boxes.

command.description: The shell command, such as "cd app && git pull && make test".

cwd.description: Working directory: relative to your home on the box, ~/..., or absolute. Default: your home.

env.description: Extra environment variables for this command only, at most 32.

timeout_seconds.description: Kill the command after this many seconds. Default 240, at most 600.

name: run_on_box

durationMs.description: How long the call took, in ms (a wake included).

stderr.description: Its stderr, cut the same way.

stdout.description: Its stdout: the first 5,000 and last 15,000 characters when longer.

timedOut.description: True when it hit timeout_seconds and was killed.

truncated.description: True when part of stdout or stderr was left out.

woke.description: True when the box was paused and was woken to run it (it bills while awake).

title: Run a command on a box
